source.title: Some open problems in control theory.

accepted.question_text: Let x'=f(x,u) be a real-analytic control system. If the system is small-time locally controllable at a state x0, must it also be small-time locally reachable at x0? The source explicitly notes that the converse implication, from small-time local reachability to small-time local controllability, is known to hold.

evidence.quote: 1) Does small time local controllability imply small time local reachability in the analytic case? (the converse holds);

accepted.question_text: In dimensions 2 and 3, suppose a control system satisfies small-time reachability together with a Lie algebra condition. Do these hypotheses imply the existence of a periodic stabilizing feedback or periodic stabilization mechanism? The source states that positive answers are already known in the other dimensions from the author's work.
accepted.context_brief: periodic stabilization in dimensions two or three

evidence.quote: 2) Does small time reachability (and a Lie algebra condition) imply periodic stabilization in dimension two or three? (the other dimensions provide positive answers due to the work of the author);

accepted.question_text: Is the one-dimensional Burgers equation globally controllable?

evidence.quote: 5) Is the one-dimensional Burgers equation globally controllable?

accepted.question_text: For a one-dimensional heat equation with a cubic nonlinearity, can the blowup phenomenon be avoided by a suitable control strategy?
accepted.context_brief: blowup avoidance for nonlinear heat equation

evidence.quote: 6)7) For a one-dimensional heat equation with cubic nonlinearity, can the blowup phenomenon be avoided? Is the equation small time controllable?

accepted.question_text: For a one-dimensional heat equation with a cubic nonlinearity, is the equation small-time controllable?
accepted.context_brief: small-time controllability for nonlinear heat equation
